fact: The Pantheon in Rome has a concrete dome, finished almost 1,900 years ago, that is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.
Roman engineers built over 80,000 kilometers of paved roads across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East—many straight enough that modern highways still follow them.
The Colosseum in Rome had a giant retractable canvas awning called the velarium, operated by sailors to shade 50,000 spectators from the sun.
Roman aqueducts used gravity alone—tilting gently by just a few centimeters per kilometer—to carry fresh water dozens of miles into cities.
Julius Caesar reformed the Roman calendar in 45 BC to create the 365-day year with a leap day every four years—the ancestor of our calendar today.
